(21 April 2010) | matches = 182 | total goals = 476 | longest wins = | longest unbeaten = | longest losses = | highest attendance = | lowest attendance = | average attendance = | prevseason = [[2009 Malaysia Super League|2009]] | nextseason = [[2011 Malaysia Super League|2011]] }} The '''2010 Liga Super''', also known as the '''TM Liga Super''' for sponsorship reasons, was the seventh season of the [[Liga Super]], the top-tier professional [[association football|football]] league in Malaysia.[https://www.rsssf.org/tablesm/malay2010.html#super - Malaysia 2010-Liga Super 2010] - [[RSSSF]] The season was held from 9 January and concluded on 3 August 2010. The [[Liga Super]] champions for 2010 was [[Selangor FA|Selangor]]. The opening match of the season between [[Negeri Sembilan FA|Negeri Sembilan]] and Selangor also doubled as the [[Piala Sumbangsih]] fixtures where it was won by Selangor by a score of 2–1. ==Team changes== The following teams have changed division. {{col-begin|width=auto}} {{col-break}} ===To Malaysia Super League=== '''Promoted from [[2009 Malaysia Premier League|Premier League]]''' * [[T-Team F.C.|T-Team]] * [[Johor FA|Johor]] * [[Kuala Lumpur FA|Kuala Lumpur]] {{col-break|gap=3em}} ===From Malaysia Super League=== '''Relegated to [[2010 Malaysia Premier League|Premier League]]''' * [[PDRM FA|PDRM]] '''Withrawal''' * [[Kuala Muda Naza F.C.|Kuala Muda Naza]] * [[UPB-MyTeam F.C.|UPB-MyTeam]] {{col-end}} ==Teams== A total of 14 teams compete in the 2010 season which includes the top 11 teams that participated in the [[2009 Liga Super|2009 season]] and champions and runners-up of the [[2009 Liga Premier]]. The three teams were promoted to complete a total 10 teams including [[2009 Liga Premier]] runners-up [[T–Team F.C.|T–Team]], third-placed [[Johor FA|Johor]] and fourth-placed [[Kuala Lumpur FA|Kuala
